A1.justification: Both complete, readable 25-page PDFs describe the same Genie Envisioner work. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic manipulation experiments on AgiBot G1, Agilex Cobot Magic and Dual Franka, alongside video-generation, simulation and human-ranking evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a pretraining/state-input ablation, RoboTwin experiments and additional baseline results.

M1.justification: The documented GE-Base, GE-Act and GE-Sim architectures, training objectives and inference procedures remain unchanged. Robot-state variants are newly analyzed in an ablation, without an explicit revision to the main method.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation into simulated manipulation with four RoboTwin tasks: grab roller, handover mic, lift pot and move can pot. It also adds a fixed-position cylinder-to-cup task for controlled analysis, substantially broadening the previously reported evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds π0 to the AgiBot G1 comparison previously containing GR00T N1 and UniVLA. GO-1 is newly evaluated specifically on RoboTwin alongside π0. Comparator membership in the retained Franka, Agilex and video-generation comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include training the ablation variants for 40,000 steps on 305 demonstrations and jointly fine-tuning one GE-Act model on 200 RoboTwin demonstrations, 50 per task. RoboTwin baselines instead use task-specific adaptation. These are added experimental settings; existing protocols and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 and new Table 1 introduce a controlled analysis crossing GE-Base initialization, task-specific video adaptation and robot-state inclusion. This substantially expands the evidence about which components support action prediction, beyond the retained slow/fast inference and metric-human consistency analyses.

E5.justification: The added results remain point estimates without new seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Section 6 retains the same three-video sampling procedure and repeated human-review description.

E6.justification: v2 adds π0 scores for five AgiBot G1 tasks, eight ablation configurations and four RoboTwin comparisons. Table 1 reports 0.89 E2E and 0.76 SR with GE-Base initialization, video adaptation and robot state. RoboTwin results favor GE-Act on three tasks but not lift pot, under differing training designs. Retained Franka, Agilex and EWMBench results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The world-model and action-model formulations, pose/motion conditioning equations and EWMBench metric definitions remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal proofs or theoretical guarantees; Figure 6's block-label correction is not a change in mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about a unified platform combining video world modeling, action prediction, simulation and evaluation. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing poorer state-conditioned performance without embodied pretraining to shortcut learning and the RoboTwin lift-pot shortfall to possible interference from joint training. Existing limitations remain unchanged. The new ablation prose ambiguously calls an improvement general video pretraining, although Table 1 defines that factor as task-specific video adaptation.

D1.justification: v2 documents demonstration counts, the 40,000-step ablation budget, joint RoboTwin training and the meanings of the ablation switches. Existing hardware descriptions, training recipes and promises of future public code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the RoboTwin 2.0 reference by Chen et al. and positions its new simulation experiment against π0 and GO-1. The related-work discussion and broader novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The revision adds an Analysis passage in Section 3.4 and a RoboTwin subsection, with a short extension to Section 4's introduction and an affiliation edit. Most existing prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 8 is redrawn with a π0 series, and v1 Figures 11 and 14 are consolidated with a RoboTwin panel into v2 Figure 11. A new ablation table is inserted and Figure 6 corrects a visual-block label. Other figures and tables are largely retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added π0 comparison, controlled ablation and RoboTwin evaluation strengthen empirical support for the retained method and generalization claims. The gain is limited by differing joint versus task-specific training in RoboTwin and the mismatch between Table 1's factor definitions and its explanatory prose. These additions improve the evidence without resolving the paper's broader evaluation limitations.
